purpose: Every CFM run on disk with its own recorded config and results, so a proposal can be checked against what is already measured before another run is launched.
source: each run's own per_epoch_metrics.{csv,json}; nothing re-derived

corpus.run_path: absolute path of the run directory
corpus.note: Wf-A115: the loader used to be REPORTS.iterdir() — one level deep — so the nested runs were structurally invisible. The corpus is therefore LARGER than the one the pre-Wf-A115 cohort medians were measured on; `by_n_train_depth1_only` keeps that earlier scope reproducible.

bond_pr_auc_definition_legend.existence_ap_v2: AP over bond EXISTENCE (score = 1 - P(NO_BOND), positive = bonded)
bond_pr_auc_definition_legend.undeclared: no definition stamped; pre-Wf-A97 artefacts measured the NO_BOND AP

runs.cohort_reason: the cohort comes from the per-epoch metrics file's own config block, which is the run of record

notes.n_epochs_run: the number of DATA ROWS in the run's per-epoch file. It is NOT the number of epochs the model trained: a run that resumed at epoch 19 has one row, and a run that early-stopped has fewer rows than its declared budget.
notes.epoch_history_contiguous_from_zero: True only when the recorded epoch indices are 0..n-1 with no gap and no offset. A resumed run starts above 0 and is therefore NOT contiguous, even though its rows are dense.
notes.history_completion_frac: epochs_recorded / epochs_declared. A value below 1.0 means the run stopped early or was killed; it is NOT a measure of training quality.

integrity.population_reason: the per-epoch file's 1 epoch(s) ARE the run of record (segment 0, 1 epoch(s) run, no extra epochs in the segment)

population_conflicts.note: Wf-A114E: the trainer writes per_epoch_metrics.json ONCE, at the end of training, to a FIXED path, so two runs launched into the same --out-dir clobber each other's record and the survivor is whichever finished LAST. events.jsonl is append-only and keeps every population, so the census now cross-checks every run against it and says, per run, WHICH population it scored and WHY. A run whose file is a truncated prefix of a longer population is re-derived from the events rows of the matching population; a run whose two records disagree irreconcilably is REFUSED and excluded from every headline population. Wf-A116: the cross-check is VALUE-AWARE — the per-epoch file is matched against the events rows of each population, so a file written by ANOTHER launch that reused the directory is not scored as if it were the run of record. `class_a_other_population` = the file is another population's record (the run of record is scored instead); `class_d_foreign_launch` = the file matches no population (the events stream is a foreign launch; the file is kept and the run is flagged UNCORROBORATED).

budget_matched.reading: end-to-end rate at epoch K-1 (final-epoch reading)
budget_matched.rule: a run contributes to budget K only if the epoch index K-1 is IN that run's own epoch sequence. A run that stopped before it does not contribute at all.
budget_matched.cohort_scope: clean runs only (contiguous from epoch 0 AND no nan train_loss), across every run the loader found
budget_matched.cohort_axis: this block is stratified on n_train ALONE.  MEASURED: the n_train=26715 cohort holds two validation protocols (see `cohort_composition`), so its median is a median over two cohorts.  The strict (n_train, n_val) cohorts are in the `by_cohort` block.
budget_matched.n_train_axis_note: No cohort median is a valid bar for the n_train axis. MEASURED: the best-epoch reading is a max over a noisy series (the census's own note: 'optimistically biased'), and the final-epoch reading is dominated by WHERE EACH COHORT STOPPED. Under the budget-matched comparison above the ordering between the two cohorts flips at the budgets listed in `flipped_budgets`, because the cohorts are out of phase in the same oscillation. The full-corpus cohort's surviving sample collapses from 9 runs at K=9 to 1 run at K=28, because its runs stopped early — a cohort median over 1 surviving run is a median over one run. Use `per_run_bar` instead.

wf_a127: MEANING CHANGED — a chemistry rate whose denominator is EMPTY is now published as null, never as the trainer's 0.0 placeholder.  There are TWO denominators in a generation-eval row: gen_validity_n (the samples the eval DREW) and gen_validity_val (the rows the eval SCORED).  The chemistry rates (gen_single_fragment_ratio, gen_largest_fragment_frac, gen_metal_ratio) are over the SCORED rows, so when the eval drew samples and NONE of them parsed they are 0/0 — undefined.  The census used to gate them on the DRAWN count, so the 0.0 placeholder was published as a measurement and the fragmentation gate FAILED on it.  MEASURED 2026-10-31 on disk: 66 of the 576 per-epoch rows across the 59 runs have gen_validity_val == 0 with gen_validity_n > 0, over 5 runs; on 2 of them it is the LAST row (cfm_fm_control_2026_10_09, cfm_bond_head_30ep_onecycle_2026_10_09).  Those two runs' fragmentation_gate moves from FAIL to SKIP / denominator_empty, and gen_single_fragment_ratio_end, gen_largest_fragment_frac_end and gen_single_molecule_rate_end move from 0.0 to null.  The convention is the trainer's own (Wf-A114/T85, molmetal/tests/test_cfm_gen_metric_sentinel.py): a rate over the SCORED rows is None when nothing was scored, the end-to-end rate inherits that undefined factor, and a rate over the DRAWN samples (gen_validity, gen_molecule_validity) stays a number — a measured 0 of N stays 0.0.
